2604:
** καταγγελ-εύς**, έως, ὁ,
**one who proclaims, herald**, ἀγώνων {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“IG” 12(2).58a10 (Mytilene, 1st c.BC),compare “BSA” 26.163 (Sparta, 2nd c.AD)}}; ξένων δαιμονίων {{NT|NT.Act.17.18.}}
2612:
** κατάδηλος**, ον,
**manifest, visible**, τούτοις οὐ κ. ἦν ἡ μάχη ὑπὸ τοῦ.. ὄρους {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.44}}; κ. γενέσθαι **to be discovered**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5, 3.68}}; κ. μᾶλλον.. τὰ τῶν Χίων ἐφάνη {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.10}}; κατάδηλον ποιῆσαι make **known, discover**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.88, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Vit.Herc.” 1457.10}}: with _participle_, φυλάσσων κ. ἔσται {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1214 (Lyric poetry); κ. γίγνονται προσποιούμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23d, etc.}}; κ. ὦσιν ὅτι.., κ. ἔσται ὡς.., {{NT+4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Prt.” 342b, 355b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 109b2, NT.Heb.7.15, etc.}} _adverb_ **-λως**{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 6.207.}}
2619:
** κατακᾰλύπτω**,
**cover up**, κατά τε κνίσῃ ἐκάλυψαν (i.e. μηρούς) {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.460, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.47 (tmesis); με τεθνηῶτα.. κατὰ γαῖα καλύπτοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.464; κατὰ δὲ σκότος ὄσσε κάλυψεν 16.325}}; Ἴδην δὲ κατὰ νεφέεσσι κ{{Refs 8th c.BC+|. 17.594; κἀμὲ θανάτου κατὰ μοῖρα καλύψαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 917 (_anapaest meter_), compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 121, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1315 (Lyric poetry), etc.:}} —_middle_, κατὰ κρᾶτα καλυψάμενος γοάασκεν **having covered his** head, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.92}}; so -καλυψάμενος alone, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.67}}; κἂν κατακεκαλυμμένος τις γνοίη even one **veiled** would perceive, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76b; λογισμῷ κατακαλυψάμενος [prev. author] “Ep.” 340a.}}
2620:
** κατακαυχάομαι**,
**boast against** one, **exult over** him, τινος {{NT+5th c.BC+|NT.Rom.11.18, Eust.ad 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta “Prooem.” p.67 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus; κατά τινος NT.Jam.3.14: _metaphorically_, -καυχᾶται ἔλεος κρίσεως [prev. work] 2.13}}; κ. ἔν τινι **to glory** in it, {{LXX|LXX.Zech.10.12.}}
2624:
** κατακληρο-δοτέω**,
**seize and parcel out**, τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν variant in {{LXX+NT|LXX.1Mac.3.36, LXX.Deu.1.38, NT.Act.13.19.}}
2628:
** κατ-ᾰκολουθ-έω**,
**follow after**, ὀπίσω τινός {{LXX+3rd c.AD+|LXX.Jer.17.16, compare 3rd c.AD(?): Longus Scriptor Eroticus 3.15 codices: with _genitive_, Dioxi pp.2 (assuming variant)}}; **comply with**, εἰ ταῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων εὐχαῖς ὁ θεὸς κατηκολούθει {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 388}}; **obey**, νόμῳ, προστάγμασιν, {{LXX+1st c.AD+|LXX.Dan.9.10, LXX.1Mac.6.23; λόγῳ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lysander” 25}}; **follow** a historical or philosophical authority, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.146 S}}.; Ἀράτῳ, Δημοκρίτῳ, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.56.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1108f; in fortification, κ. ταῖς ὀχυρότησι τῶν τόπων 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.42.2}}; **emulate, imitate**, ἀδυνάτοις ἐπιβολαῖς Hegetorap.{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Cit. 3}}; κ. τοῖς ἱεροῖς, mistranslation of **prosecuisset**, as though **prosecutus esset**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 5}}: _absolutely_, **obey instructions,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|PAmh. 2.31.12 (2nd c.BC).}}
2645:
** κατάλοιπος**, ον,
**left remaining**, τὸ κ. ἀπεργάζεσθαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 39e}}; ἐκ τοῦ κ. {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 548b18, compare “Michel” 829.23 (1st c.BC)}}, etc.; τὰ κ. τῆς διεξόδου {{Refs 5th c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.120 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus}}; τοῦτο.. κατάλοιπόν [ἐστι] with _infinitive_, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC(?): Strato Comicus 1.10; ἡ κ. εἰσβολή 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.91.9}}; ἡ κ. the **other** of two, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.314.}}
2646:
** κατάλῠμα**, ατος, τό,
**lodging**, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.36.1 (_plural_), “UPZ” 120.5 (2nd c.BC), LXX.Exo.4.24, Aristeas 181 (_plural_), NT.Mark.14.14, 2nd c.AD: Iamblichus Scriptor Eroticus 13}}; δημόσιον κ. {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.93}}; **billet** for troops, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PSI” 4.341.8 (3rd c.BC)}}: in _plural_, **provision of quarters,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|Inscriptiones Graecae 5(2).515 (Lycosura, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD)}}:—_diminutive_ **κατ-λῠμάτιον**, τό, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PCair.Zen.” 205 (3rd c.BC).}}
2651:
** καταμόνᾱς**,
_adverb_ **alone, apart**, better divisim κατὰ μόνας, see at {μόνος} {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.}}
2652:
** κατανά-θεμα**, ατος, τό,
**curse,** {{NT|NT.Rev.22.3}}; and **κατανα-θεμᾰτίζω**, **curse,** NT.Mat.26.74, both variants for καταθ-.
2653:
Included with: ** κατανά-θεμα**, ατος, τό,
**curse,** {{NT|NT.Rev.22.3}}; and **κατανα-θεμᾰτίζω**, **curse,** NT.Mat.26.74, both variants for καταθ-.
2656:
** κατανεύω**,
_future_ **-νεύσομαι** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.524, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “R.” 350e}}: _aorist_ {{Refs 8th c.BC+|κατένευσα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.558}}, etc.; _Epic dialect_ _participle_ {{Refs 8th c.BC+|καννεύσας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.464}}:—**nod assent**, [{{Refs 8th c.BC+|κεφαλῇ κατανεύσομαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.524; Χαίταις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.14; κατανεύσομαι καὶ ἀνανεύσομαι Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “R.” [same place], compare “Euthd.” 277c, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ec.” 72: _absolutely_, of granting a request, ὑπέστην καὶ κατένευσα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.267, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.111, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Th.” 1020:}}] with _accusative_ _of things_, **grant, promise**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|ὅτι μοι κατένευσε Κρονίων νίκην καὶ μέγα κῦδος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.175}}: later with _dative_, **consent to**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“BGU” 1119.24 (1st c.BC)}}: with _future_ _infinitive_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|δωσέμεναι κατένευσε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.393; ὑπέσχετο καὶ κατένευσεν Ἴλτον ἐκπέρσαντ᾽ εὐτείχεον ἀπονέεσθαι 2.112}}: later with _aorist_ _infinitive_, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus “fragment” 5.8}}: generally, **make a signbynoddingthehead**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|ὁ δὲ τῇ -ένευσε σιωπῇ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.463}}.
**II** **bow down**, εἰς γῆν variant in {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 7.14; ἐπειδὰν -νεύσῃ τὸ ἀγγεῖον “Geoponica” 2.4.2; κ. τὴν κεφαλήν 2nd c.AD: Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.205}}: _perfect_ _participle_ -νενευκώς **downcast**, {{Refs|Vett. Val. 2.4.}}
**III** Astron., **tilt downward**, of the pole, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus “Ars” 6.31. [κατᾱνεύων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.490}}.]
2660:
** κατα-νύσσω**,
**stab, gouge**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς τινος 2nd c.AD: Phlegon Trallianus Paradoxographus 36.4J.}}:—elsewhere in _passive_, with _future_ **-νῠγήσομαι** {{LXX|Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Sir.20.21}}: _aorist_ -ενύγην [ῠ] (see. below); **to be sorely pricked**, _metaphorically_, {{LXX|κατενύγησαν τὴν καρδίαν “Act.Ap.” 2.37, cf. LXX.Gen.34.7}}: hence, **to be bewildered, stunned**, {{LXX|κάθισον -νενυγμένη Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Isa.47.5, cf. LXX.Psa.4.5}}, +others; **keep silence**, {{LXX|LXX.Lev.10.3.}}
2662:
** καταπᾰτ-έω**,
**trample under foot**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.84, etc.; ὑσὶ τὸ σπέρμα κ}}. **trample down** the seed (i.e. _have_ it _trampled down_) by swine, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.14:}} —_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev\. author] 7.173, 223, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.72, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.37; τὸν ἐγκέφαλον ἐν ταῖς πτέρναις -πεπατημένον φορεῖν [prev\. author] 7.45}}.
**2** _metaphorically_, [{{NT+8th c.BC+|κατὰ δ᾽ ὅρκια πιστὰ πάτησαν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.157; κ. τοὺς νόμους Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Leges” 714a; τὰ γράμματα [prev\. author] “Grg.” 484a; τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ NT.Heb.10.29; ὅρκον 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Epistulae” 14.1}}].
2663:
** κατά-παυσις**, εως, ἡ,
**stopping**: _metaphorically_, **putting down, deposing**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|τυράννων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.38}}; τῆς βασιληΐης **deposition** from.., [{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|[prev\. author] 6.67; Κολλατίνου Dio Cassius Historicus [{2-3rd c.AD}] 46.49}}].
**II** **rest, calm**, {{LXX|LXX.Isa.66.1}}, +others; **place of rest**, [{{LXX+4-3rd c.BC+|LXX.Psa.94(95).11, +others; αἱ κ. τῶν πνευμάτων Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “de Ventis” 18}}]: _metaphorically_, **allaying**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|στάσεως 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.86}} K.
2670:
** καταποντ-ίζω**,
**throw into the sea, plunge** or **drown therein**, τινα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.27, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.169, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.403c, etc.: _metaphorically_, 4th-3rd c.BC: Axiopistus Poeta Ethicus 6 (_passive_); κ. τὰς βουλάς 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 49.10}}:—_passive_, variant in [{{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.60.8; καταποντισθεὶς ὑπὸ τῆς θαλάσσης 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 18.20; ἐν τῷ πελάγει NT.Matt.18.6; εἰς τὸ πέλαγος Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Timoleon” 13}}]; **sink,** NT.Mat.14.30; of a ship, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PPetr.” 2p.135 (3rd c.BC).}}
2671:
** κατ-άρα** [ᾰρ],
_Ionic dialect_ **κατ-άρη**, ἡ, **curse**, κατάρας ποιέεσθαί τινι to lay **curses** upon one, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.165; ἐποιήσαντο νόμον τε καὶ κατάρην μὴ.. θρέψειν κόμην.. μηδένα [prev. work] 82; ἐκ κατάρης τευ in consequence of.., [prev\. author] 4.30; διδόναι τινὰ κατάρᾳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 945 (Lyric poetry), compare “El.” 1324 (_plural_, _anapaest meter_), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Th.” 725 (_plural_, Lyric poetry); opposed to εὐχή, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Alc.” 2.143b (_plural_), compare “SIG” 1241 (Lyttus, 3rd c.AD), etc.; opposed to εὐλογία, NT.Jam.3.10; κατάραι γίγνονται κατά τινος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 23.10.7}}; τὴν κ. ἀναγράψαι, στηλιτεῦσαι, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.45, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus}} 2.354b; **cursing**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|κ. καὶ λοιδορία 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.11}} O.
2672:
** καταρ-άομαι** [ᾱρ
_Epic dialect_, ᾰρ _Attic dialect_], **call down curses upon**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|τῷ δὲ κατᾱρῶνται πάντες βροτοὶ ἄλγε᾽ ὀπίσσω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.330}}; πολλὰ κατηρᾶτο he **called down** many **curses**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.454; κεφαλῇ πολλὰ κ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.39; κ. ὁ κῆρυξ εἴ τις ἐξαπατᾷ λέγων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.97; κ. τὴν Ἶσίν τινι “AP” 11.115 (1st c.AD: Nicarchus Epigrammaticus)}}: with _infinitive_, καταρῶνται δ᾽ ἀπολέσθαι they **pray** that he may perish, {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 277; κ. μήτε πλοῖα στεγανὰ γενέσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “fragment” 554, compare 148: with _dative_}}, **curse, execrate**, {{NT+5th c.BC+|τῷ ἡλίῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.184, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nu.” 871, “Ra.” 746, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.292 codices, etc.: with _accusative_, LXX.Gen.12.3, +others, “NT.Mark.11.21”, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 32 codices, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 27: _absolutely_, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “V.” 614, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283:—}}_passive_, _aorist_ κατηράθην [ᾱ] {{LXX|LXX.Job.3.5}}: _perfect_ _participle_ κατηραμένος **accursed**, {{NT+1st c.AD+|[prev. work] “4 Ki.” 9.34, “NT.Mat.25.41”, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Luc.” 18}}: also _perfect_ κεκατήραμαι with double _reduplicate_, {{LXX|LXX.Num.22.6}}; _participle_ κεκατηραμένος {{LXX|LXX.Sir.3.18, +others}}
2675:
** καταρτ-ίζω**,
**adjust, put in order, restore**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|πάντα ἐς τὠυτό 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106}}; Μίλητος νοσήσασα στάσι, μέχρι οὗ μιν Πάριοι κατήρτισαν [{{Refs 1st c.AD+|[prev. work] 28, compare 30; τὸν δῆμον Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Marcellus” 10}}]; ἵνα καταρτισθῇ [ἡ πόλις] {{NT+1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.10; κ. δίκτυα _mend,_ NT.Matt.4.21}}; **set** a dislocated limb, in _passive_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Apollonius Citiensis Medicus 2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Heliodorus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 49.1.3 (_active_ and _passive_); but κ. τὴν ὀσφὺν καὶ τοὺς ὤμους}} **form** them by exercise, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epict.” 3.20.10: _metaphorically_}}, **restore to a right mind,** NT.Gal.6.1; [{{Refs 1st c.AD+|κ. τινὰ εἰς τὸ συμφέρον Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Cat.Mi.” 65}}]; **reconcile**, {{Refs 4th c.AD+|φίλους διαφερομένους 4th c.AD: Eusebius Myndius Philosophus 1}}; **make good**, {{Refs|τὰ ὑστερήματα τῆς πίστεως “1st Epistle to the Thessalonians” 3.10}}:—_middle_, {{LXX|ἠσθένησε, σὺ δὲ κατηρτίσω αὐτήν Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Psa.67(68).10}}.
**II** **furnish, equip**, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|τετρήρη πληρώματι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.47.6, +others, compare “PTeb.” 6.7 (2nd c.BC, _passive_), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.70, etc.:}} —_passive_, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|πλοῖα ταῖς εἰρεσίαις κατηρτισμένα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.2.11}}; κατηρτισμένος _absolutely_, **in battle array**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.66}}; **instructed,** NT.Luke.6.40; **prepare, make ready**, [{{Refs 3rd c.BC+|σφενδόνην Philo Mechanicus [{3-2nd c.BC}] “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 78.24}}]:—_middle_, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Exo.15.17, +others: σῶμα κατηρτίσω μοι NT.Heb.10.5; ὁ τὸν κόσμον καταρτισάμενος “PMag.Par.” 1.1147}}: with _infinitive_, {{Refs|κατηρτίσατο δίδοσθαι “OGI” 177.10}} (Egypt, 1st c.BC):—so in _passive_, {{NT+1st c.BC+|[prev. work]179.8 ([prev. passage], 1st c.BC): _absolutely_ in _imperative_, καταρτίζεσθε NT.2Cor.13.11}}.
**II.2** **compound, prepare** dishes, medicines, etc., {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Alex.Praef.” codices (see. καταρτύω):}} —_middle_, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Th.” 954.}}
2679:
** κατασκάπτω**,
_perfect_ **-έσκᾰφα** [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|Isocrates Orator [{5-6th c.BC}] 14.35}}]:—**dig down**, [{{Refs 3rd c.BC+|ἐπὶ θάτερα τῆς ἀμπέλου Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “Historia Plantarum” 4.13.5}}]; but usually,
**II** **destroy utterly, raze to the ground**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|τὸ ἄστυ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.156; Τροίαν κ. βίᾳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 998, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Ag.” 525; πάτραν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1421; δόμους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 566; πόλιν “SIG” 344.7}} (Teos, [{{LXX+6th c.BC+|4th c.BC), compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.71; το τέγος Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Nubes” 1488; τὰ τείχη ἐς ἔδαφος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.109, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.40, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator [same place], 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ath.” 37.1; τὸν λιμένα 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.123; τὰ θυσιαστήρια Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.1Ki.19.10; τὴν οἰκίαν εἰς ἔδαφος Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Publicola” 10}}], etc.:—_passive_, {{Refs|ϝοικία κατασκαπτέσθω “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.8}} (_Locrian dialect_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC); τὰ οἱκία οἱ κατεσκάφη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.72; πατρῴα ἑστία κατεσκάφη 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 22; τὰ κατεσκαμμένα ἀναστήσω Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum “Amos” 9.11}}.
2681:
** κατασκην-όω**,
**take up one's quarters, encamp**, εἰς.. [{{LXX+6th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cyr.” 4.5.39, “Hell.Oxy.” 16.2, etc.; ἐν.. LXX.1Ch.23.25; ἔνθα κατεσκηνώκατε Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.2}}]: generally, **rest**, {{LXX|ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Psa.15(16).9}}; **settle**, of birds, {{NT|ἐν κλάδοις NT.Matt.13.32}}: _metaphorically_, {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|οὐ ψυχὴ ἐν μόνῳ ἀνθρώπῳ κ. 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 4.9}}.
2682:
